record.paper_title: On some open problems of number theory
record.original_question: For every integer n > 1, does the equation 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z have a solution in positive integers x, y, and z?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Prove or disprove: for every integer $n > 1$, there exist positive integers $x, y, z$ (not necessarily distinct) such that
$$\frac{4}{n} = \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{z}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Erdős–Straus conjecture remains open in general. It has been verified computationally for all n up to very large bounds (at least 10^17), and density results show the set of exceptions has density zero, but no proof for all n > 1 is known.

status_evidence.title: Erdős–Straus conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture states that 4/n can be written as a sum of three unit fractions for every n ≥ 2. It remains unproven.
